headline: Kai, the hot PCE print locked in a December hike — and the Dow still clawed back an 1,100-point loss by the close.
subline: Markets are closed for Thanksgiving after a wild Wednesday; Brent sits near $95 on fresh Saudi strike reports and bitcoin is back above $60,000.
asof: Markets closed for Thanksgiving, Friday ends at 1 PM ET · Wednesday's closes, bitcoin live as of 6:40 AM ET · every figure links to its source below

items.title: Hot core PCE cements a December rate hike
items.sentence: October core PCE rose 3.3% year over year, above the 3.2% consensus, and CME FedWatch odds of a December hike reached 97.8%, per Capp Notes.

items.title: Dow erases an 1,100-point intraday loss
items.sentence: Stocks staged a late comeback Wednesday as the Dow closed up 0.33% and most S&P 500 names rose, even with Nvidia down 3.91%, per The Motley Fool.

items.title: US proposes tariffs on 14 trading partners
items.sentence: Washington announced Section 301 "overproduction" tariffs targeting 14 economies including South Korea, China, the EU and Japan, per SBS News and Capp Notes.

items.title: Oil climbs again on Saudi strike reports
items.sentence: Brent rose 3.51% to $94.61 and WTI 1.99% to $83.68 after a reported Houthi strike on the Ras Tanura complex, per Capp Notes.

items.title: Bitcoin steadies back above $60,000
items.sentence: Bitcoin trades near $60,600 this morning, up about 3.5% in 24 hours after a $264 million liquidation flush hit shorts hardest, per CoinDesk and The Crypto Times.

items.title: Macy's parade celebrates 100 years in Manhattan
items.sentence: The Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade marks 100 years as it rolls through New York this morning, per NBC News.

items.title: AAA expects 81.5 million Thanksgiving travelers
items.sentence: AAA projects 81.5 million Americans traveling 50 miles or more through Monday, with the TSA screening nearly 17.6 million flyers, per Good Morning America.

items.title: Houthis press campaign against Saudi oil sites
items.sentence: The Houthis have claimed strikes on Ras Tanura, Rabigh and Abqaiq in recent weeks, a campaign Oilprice.com calls a major driver of crude prices.

items.title: Russian bombers skirt South Korean airspace
items.sentence: Moscow released footage of Tu-160 bombers that flew unusually close to airspace above Ulleungdo in the East Sea earlier this week, per SBS News.

items.title: Asia's sell-off ran deeper than Wall Street's
items.sentence: South Korea's Kospi fell 6.16% and Taiwan's Taiex 4.80% on Wednesday as the AI unwind went global, per Capp Notes.

items.title: Lab staff reportedly uneasy about unreleased models
items.sentence: More than two dozen sources told Axios that some OpenAI and Anthropic employees worry certain unreleased models may be too powerful to release safely, per DIGITIMES.

items.title: GPT-6 designs proteins that bind in the lab
items.sentence: OpenAI says GPT-6 designed protein sequences that showed binding evidence against five targets in wet-lab experiments, per The Neuron.

items.title: Claude artifacts become installable desktop apps
items.sentence: Anthropic shipped desktop-app installs for artifacts on Mac and Windows and announced Skills over MCP on the protocol's second anniversary, per The Neuron.

items.title: Amazon catches an AI agent exploiting a zero-day
items.sentence: Amazon researchers detected an open-source AI agent exploiting a previously unknown vulnerability with limited human intervention, per The Neuron.

items.title: US blacklists Megaspeed as chip scrutiny widens
items.sentence: Washington blacklisted Nvidia-linked Megaspeed while Jensen Huang still faces congressional scrutiny over chip export controls, per The Neuron.
